display.title: Simcha Power: The Chassid Who Danced on Simchas Torah
display.summary_short: Serving Hashem with joy, the Rebbeim who daven for Chassidim before trouble comes, and a Chassid of the Tzemach Tzedek whose Simchas Torah dancing saves his sick son.
display.summary_long: The storyteller teaches that we must serve Hashem with simcha, like a birthday present wrapped with love. A bad mood is like a passing cloud, and he shares a doctor's advice: 'Some days you feel good, and some days you feel better.' On the anniversary of the Rebbe and Rebbetzin's wedding, he tells how the Rebbe Rashab would take out a Chassid's old letter and daven for him when he sensed a cloud over him, how the Frierdiker Rebbe did the same, and how the Rebbe asked his secretary to keep an index of Chassidim's names. Then the main story: a Chassid of the Tzemach Tzedek, whose son is gravely ill, reaches Lubavitch on Hoshana Rabbah and hears only 'Hashem should help.' He spends the day saying Tehillim in tears. The storyteller explains the Rebbe's teaching, said forty years earlier on Shabbos Vayishlach, that in our generation simcha and bitachon bring blessing. When Shemini Atzeres begins, the Chassid puts down his Tehillim and dances with all his might through Simchas Torah. Before he leaves, the Tzemach Tzedek tells him that his joy broke a Heavenly decree, and at home his son greets him, healthy.
display.lesson: Serve Hashem with joy; even when you are not in the mood, act b'simcha and you will become happy, and simcha brings Hashem's blessings.

date.note: 'Today is the anniversary of the Rebbe and the Rebbetzin... Yud-Daled Kislev'; the maamar of Shabbos Vayishlach 5746 was 'exactly 40 years ago... this coming Shabbos, tomorrow night'.

advisories.note: A boy is gravely ill and doctors expect him to die; he recovers completely.
